title: a lot much many
subtitle: much money / many books
summary: Use much with uncountable nouns, many with plural nouns, and a lot of with both kinds of noun.

left.label: much + uncountable noun
left.text: much food, much money, much luggage.
examples: *A:* Have you got any money? *B:* I've got some, but **not much**.

right.label: many + plural noun
right.text: many books, many people, many photos.
examples: *A:* Did you take any photos? *B:* I took some, but **not many**.

lesson.heading: a lot of + both types of noun
lesson.text: **a lot of** goes with uncountable nouns *and* plural nouns. With an uncountable noun the verb is singular; with a plural noun the verb is plural.

examples.text: We bought **a lot of food** and **a lot of books**.
Paula hasn't got **a lot of** free **time**.
There **is** a lot of **food** on the table.
There **are** a lot of **shops** in this street.

lesson.heading: Which word can I use?
rows: We've got **many / a lot of** friends.

lesson.heading: much in questions and negatives
lesson.text: We use **much** in *questions* and *negative sentences*. We do not often use **much** in positive sentences. Use **a lot of** instead.

examples.text: Do you drink **much coffee**? I don't drink **much coffee**.

lesson.heading: many and a lot of are free
lesson.text: **many** and **a lot of** are fine in all types of sentence: positive, negative and question.

examples.text: We've got **many** friends / **a lot of** friends.
We haven't got **many** friends / **a lot of** friends.
Have you got **many** friends / **a lot of** friends?

lesson.heading: much and a lot without a noun
lesson.text: You can use **much** and **a lot** alone, with no noun after them.

examples.text: Donna spoke to me, but she didn't say **much**.
'Do you watch TV **much**?' 'No, **not much**.' (= not often)
We like films, so we go to the cinema **a lot**.

lesson.text: Can you count it? *books, people, photos* -> **many**. Can't you count it? *money, food, time* -> **much**. **a lot of** always works.

exercises.explanation: food is uncountable, so much food.

exercises.prompt: There aren't ___ hotels in this town.
exercises.explanation: hotels is a plural noun, so many hotels.

exercises.prompt: Does each noun go after much or after many?
___ people are coming to the party?
exercises.explanation: people is plural, so How many.

exercises.prompt: ___ milk do you want in your coffee?
exercises.explanation: milk is uncountable, so How much.
time is uncountable and the sentence is negative, so much time.

exercises.prompt: I know Tokyo well. I've been there ___ .
exercises.explanation: times is plural, so many times.

exercises.prompt: This road is very dangerous. There are ___ here.
exercises.explanation: a lot of works with plural nouns: a lot of accidents.
We do not often use much in positive sentences, so a lot of tea.

exercises.statement: It costs much money to travel around the world.
exercises.explanation: It costs a lot of money to travel around the world. much is not natural in a positive sentence.
'Yes, a lot.' We do not say Yes, much.

exercises.prompt: Jim loves films. Write what he does. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: He goes to the cinema a lot.
exercises.explanation: We say go to the cinema a lot, not go to the cinema much.
